title: Nested declared-results `if` inside an enclosing `if` arm emits an unspendable locking script (issue #149, OPEN at HEAD, all 7 tiers byte-identical)
repro: cd packages/runar-testing && sed -i '' "s/describe.skip('OPEN: nested/describe('OPEN: nested/" src/__tests__/nested-declared-results-arm-layout-vm.test.ts && npx vitest run src/__tests__/nested-declared-results-arm-layout-vm.test.ts
mechanism: An inner `if` that merges a local in both arms declares results; adopting a declared result ROLL+DROPs the stale slot, and the scan covers the whole arm stack including the region inherited from the ENCLOSING arm. lowerIf then reconciles by name-set and by depth, and both agree — only the LAYOUT differs. The two outer paths leave equal depth with different layouts and all post-OP_ENDIF code is generated against one of them.
consequence: A contract using the extremely common shape `if (a) { if (b) { x = ..; } else { x = ..; } }` compiles to a locking script whose else path fails OP_VERIFY. The UTXO is permanently unspendable: funds loss. Verified failing on @bsv/sdk Spend in both fold modes (PC 710). All seven compilers emit byte-identical bytes for it, so cross-tier parity is green on the broken script.
proposed_fix: Teach lowerIf's reconcile about an arm that rearranged slots it inherited: compare arm-exit LAYOUT (slot identity order), not just name-set and depth. Ship in all 7 tiers with a fixture + witness.

title: Same nested-`if` defect ALSO produces a wrongly-SPENDABLE script — the guard is bypassed, not just locked; this consequence is undocumented
mechanism: Same layout-rotation defect as CC-001. Where CC-001's wrong layout makes a true guard evaluate false, the mirror case makes a false guard evaluate true: post-OP_ENDIF `OP_ROT OP_ROT OP_LESSTHAN` compares two operands that the then-path and else-path placed at different depths.
consequence: A 36-byte contract whose only spending condition is `assert(br0 < sib0)` is spendable with param2=0, 1, or -1, all of which the source semantics REJECT. Anyone can spend the UTXO without satisfying the contract's guard. docs/test-skips.md:111 documents only the locked-funds direction ('the else path fails OP_VERIFY and locks funds'), so the open issue's recorded severity understates it: this is an authorization bypass, not only an availability loss. All 6 native tiers emit byte-identical hex.
proposed_fix: Same fix as CC-001; add this direction as a second regression fixture so a partial fix that only repairs the OP_VERIFY case cannot pass.

title: The only absolute execution oracles in the fuzz loop (--execute, --tri-modal) generate no `if` statement at all — the entire branch family has zero randomized absolute-oracle coverage
repro: grep -n "kind: 'if'" packages/runar-testing/src/fuzzer/generator.ts | sed -n '1,99p'  # none inside arbExecMethodBody's emitted body
mechanism: arbExecMethodBody emits only var_decls, an optional ForStmt, ByteString decls, and a terminal assert. Branch shapes (BRANCH_SHAPES / arbBranchBlockIR) exist only in arbGeneratedContract / arbGeneratedStatefulContract, which drive `--ir` mode — a cross-TIER parity comparison, not an absolute oracle. Parity is definitionally blind to a defect all seven tiers share, and CC-001/CC-002 are exactly that.
consequence: Every branch-merge miscompilation the project has shipped and fixed (branch-merged-locals, state-framing, and open #149) was outside the reachable space of the only randomized oracle that could have caught it. Patching arbExecMethodBody to emit a nested branch plus a non-commutative terminal read (audits/v1-review/claude/repro/CC-exec-branch-generator.patch, ~80 lines) makes --tri-modal find CC-002 in 39 property runs, and 8/8 fresh seeds diverge within 7-52 runs.
proposed_fix: Land the patch (or equivalent): draw an optional branch block in arbExecMethodBody covering flat-if, if-else, and nested declared-results-in-arm, with a live sibling local declared after the merged local.

title: Terminal assert clauses in the execution-oracle generator are commutative in the merged locals, so a pure slot SWAP is invisible to the verdict comparison
repro: With the CC-003 patch but the terminal clause written as `br0 + sib0 !== acc + 987654n`, --tri-modal --num 2000 --seed 99 passes; changing that one clause to the non-commutative `br0 <cmp> sib0` fails at run 39.
mechanism: arbCarrierClause / arbExtraClause build comparisons like `acc + wacc <cmp> rhs` and `acc - 4n < (0n - prop) - acc`. Addition is commutative, so a miscompile that reads two merged locals from each other's slots leaves the clause's value unchanged and the verdict identical. The oracle reports agreement on a script that read the wrong stack slots.
consequence: Even after branches are reachable, a whole class of layout defects (pairwise slot rotation) stays undetectable. This was measured directly: the same generator patch found nothing in 2000 runs with a commutative clause and failed in 39 with a non-commutative one.
proposed_fix: Require at least one order-sensitive comparison between distinct merged locals in every generated terminal assert (`a <cmp> b`, or `a * K + b`).

title: Golden-provenance gate accepts an allowlist entry that declares itself unreviewed; 27 of 210 shipped entries do exactly that
repro: see audits/v1-review/claude/logs/10-gate-golden-provenance.log (experiment G2): corrupt a golden byte, append an entry with reviewer='unreviewed:generated-by-agent' and reason='AUDIT PROBE: no verification whatsoever was performed', gate exits 0
mechanism: entryProblems() requires only that `reviewer` be a non-empty string and `reason` be >= 8 characters. The `review-status` field is never read. Twenty-seven live entries carry reviewer='unreviewed:generated-by-agent' AND review-status='unreviewed' and are accepted as provenance justification.
consequence: The gate that exists because goldens are self-produced by the implementation under test can be satisfied by a machine-written string. A regenerated golden that encodes a miscompilation passes with an entry that literally records that nobody checked it.
proposed_fix: Reject entries whose review-status is 'unreviewed' or whose reviewer matches /^unreviewed:/, and burn down the 27 existing ones. Optionally require `verified-against: official-KAT|differential-oracle` to name a test file that exists.

title: 91% of execution-oracle spends are rejections, so the oracle mostly compares trivially-agreeing failures
repro: cd conformance && node_modules/.bin/tsx fuzzer/index.ts --execute --num 6000 --seed 20260810   # -> Spends run: 71160 (accept=6633 reject=64527)
mechanism: Method args are drawn from |value| <= EXEC_INT_MAG = 8n and ByteStrings are fixed at 4 bytes, while the generated terminal assert conjoins several independently-drawn comparisons. The conjunction is false for most draws, so both engines reject and agree for the uninteresting reason.
consequence: The headline corpus size overstates the real signal by ~10x: only 6633 of 71160 spends exercised an accepting path through the compiled script. Boundary integers named in the review (2^31-1, 2^31, 2^32, 2^64) are never drawn at all.
proposed_fix: Bias arbExecValue toward values that satisfy the drawn guard (solve/retry), and widen the literal domain to include script-number boundary magnitudes.

title: Assignment to a `readonly` property is accepted by all 7 tiers although spec/semantics.md defines it as an ERROR; the resulting locking script has no authorization at all
repro: audits/v1-review/claude/repro/Hijack.runar.py — compilers/go/runar-go --source Hijack.runar.py --hex  =>  76a97ca9788777  (same on rust/python/java; the .runar.ts form compiles on all 7)
mechanism: spec/semantics.md:247 gives the rule `<this.p = e, env, sigma> ==> ERROR: cannot assign to readonly property` and spec/grammar.md:94 says readonly properties `cannot be reassigned`. Neither 02-validate.ts nor 03-typecheck.ts implements that rule — validate only checks that a stateless contract HAS no mutable property, never that a readonly one is not WRITTEN. The write is lowered as a local rebind, so every later read of the property sees the assigned value instead of the constructor value embedded in the script.
consequence: A contract that reassigns its readonly owner before checking it compiles to `OP_DUP OP_HASH160 OP_SWAP OP_HASH160 OP_OVER OP_EQUAL OP_NIP` — 7 bytes that compare hash160(pk) against hash160(pk) and are therefore true for ANY pubkey. The deployed owner constructor arg is never referenced. Anyone can spend. Reproduced identically from the .runar.ts and .runar.py surfaces, so the `tsc would flag it` argument does not cover the other 8 syntaxes. Interpreter and VM AGREE on the invented semantics, so every differential oracle in the repo reports green: this is H5's shared-misreading case with the spec text available in-repo.
proposed_fix:
Implement the spec rule in 02-validate.ts: error on any AssignmentExpression whose target is `this.

` where p.readonly, outside the constructor. Port to all 7 tiers and add a negative fixture to the cross-tier reject-parity set.

title: Non-literal property initializer: rust/zig/python/ruby ACCEPT a program ts/go/java reject
mechanism: CLAUDE.md and the TS golden restrict property initializers to literal values (BigIntLiteral / BoolLiteral / ByteStringLiteral). ts, go and java enforce it ('Property p initializer must be a literal value'); rust, zig, python and ruby do not and compile the expression, emitting byte-identical hex among themselves.
consequence: Four of seven tiers emit a deployable locking script for a program the language does not define. A developer using the Rust/Zig/Python/Ruby CLI gets an artifact; the same source is a hard compile error under TS/Go/Java, so the tiers disagree about what the language IS. Nothing catches it: no conformance fixture exercises a non-literal initializer, and the parity runner only compares tiers on fixtures that all of them accept.
proposed_fix: Add the literal-only initializer check to rust/zig/python/ruby validate passes; add N10 to a cross-tier NEGATIVE conformance set that asserts identical rejection, which does not exist today.

title: 18 tests report as passing while asserting nothing — an early return the silent-skip linter cannot see
repro: see audits/v1-review/claude/logs/13-vacuous-tests.log — replacing the two `return;` statements with a throw turns 18 of the file's 106 'passing' tests red
mechanism: Both describes build paths as `conformance/tests/<dir>/<dir>.runar.rs`. Fixture sources moved out to `examples/<lang>/<dir>/<ContractName>.runar.<ext>` (referenced via `conformance/tests/<dir>/source.json`), so `existsSync(path)` is false for all 9 entries and every test returns before its first expect(). A second guard in the same file (`if (rsResult.errors.some(e => e.severity === 'error')) return;`) would also silently pass a genuine Rust-parser failure.
consequence: The repo's skip accounting (134 sites / 66 inventory rows, gated by lint-no-silent-skips.sh + audit-test-skips.py) claims every skip is documented. These 18 are not skips by the linter's definition and are absent from the inventory, so 'Rust parser parses the conformance corpus' and 'Rust and TS produce matching contract structure' are green claims backed by nothing.
proposed_fix: Resolve the sources through source.json (as the conformance runner does) and make a missing file or a parse error a hard failure. Add an assertion-count or `expect.hasAssertions()` style check so a vacuous test cannot report green.

title: The independent oracle for every Go-only proof-system primitive (tests/vectors/*.json) sits outside the golden-provenance gate
repro: node conformance/scripts/check-golden-provenance.mjs --files tests/vectors/babybear_mul.json,tests/vectors/bn254_pairing.json  =>  'no golden/vector files changed — nothing to justify' (exit 0)
mechanism: GOLDEN_MATCHERS covers conformance/runtime-vectors/*.json but not tests/vectors/*.json. Those files are the Plonky3 (p3-baby-bear / p3-koala-bear / p3-poseidon2) and gnark-crypto derived vectors that are the ONLY independent oracle for BabyBear, KoalaBear, Poseidon2, BN254 and FRI — the families that are Go-only by policy and therefore have definitionally vacuous cross-tier parity.
consequence: A silent hand-edit to the vectors that back the Go-only crypto is unjustified-free, and the generators are not re-run in CI to diff them. Relatedly, bn254_pairing.json carries only 4 vectors for the single most security-critical operation in the Groth16 path.
proposed_fix: Add `(p) => /^tests\/vectors\/.*\.json$/.test(p)` to GOLDEN_MATCHERS, and add a CI step that re-runs tests/generate-vectors and git-diffs the output (the same mechanism decompiler fingerprints already use).

title: The cross-tier canonicalJson fuzzer silently degrades from 7 tiers to 6 and still reports 'complete, 0 mismatches, exit 0'
repro: cd conformance && node_modules/.bin/tsx fuzzer/index.ts --canonical --num 300 --seed 313373  =>  'Mismatches: 0 ... Tiers: ts=ok go=ok rust=ok python=ok zig=skip ruby=ok java=ok', exit 0
mechanism: When a tier's canonicalise shim binary is absent the harness marks it `skip`, excludes it from the comparison, and neither warns nor fails. The Zig shim needs a separate `zig build canonicalise` step that the workflow performs as its own build step; if that step is removed, renamed or silently fails, the nightly wire-parity job still passes with Zig unchecked.
consequence: canonicalJson is a wire-protocol primitive: a tier that disagrees on one byte breaks every cross-tier signature. The gate that is supposed to establish 7-tier byte parity can report success having established 6-tier parity, and the report gives no non-zero signal.
proposed_fix: Add a `--require-tiers` (default: all 7) that exits non-zero when any expected tier is skipped, and set it in the nightly job.

title: The replayable fuzz-regression corpus does not catch either HEAD-fixed miscompilation; only the fixtures the fixes shipped with do
repro: see audits/v1-review/claude/logs/70-revert-proof-state.log — git checkout 23ef2d2b~1 -- packages/runar-sdk/src/state.ts && pnpm --filter runar-sdk build, then: --replay 5/5 PASS; sdk-output 1 FAIL; state-push-framing-vm 9 FAIL; runar-sdk 13 FAIL
mechanism: conformance/fuzz-regressions/entries/ holds 5 entries (3 shift/bitwise, 1 byte-semantics, 1 branch-k1 guard bypass). Neither the branch-merged-locals nor the state-framing bug of e7221a7 has an entry, because neither was found by a fuzzer — the randomized oracles cannot reach those shapes (CC-003).
consequence: The corpus that is described as 'what keeps a divergence the fuzzer already found from having to be rediscovered by chance' contains nothing for the two miscompilations the release candidate exists to fix. Their only regression protection is the hand-written fixture and pinned VM test each fix shipped with — real, but single-shape and not replayable against a mutated compiler.
proposed_fix: Promote the minimized CC-002 counterexample (and the #149 reduction) into conformance/fuzz-regressions/entries/ so both branch-layout defects replay on every CI run.

title: `--spend-oracle` — the repo's only ABSOLUTE + full-tx-context + state-VALUE oracle — had never been executed, and its branch-shape space cannot express the open S0 (0 failures in 11,750 spend inputs)
repro: cd conformance && node_modules/.bin/tsx fuzzer/index.ts --spend-oracle --num 4000 --seed 777001   # -> Cases 4000/4000, Spend inputs 11750, Failures 0. Then apply audits/v1-review/claude/repro/CC-013-nested-sibling-generator.patch and re-run --num 200 at seeds 111/222/333/444 -> 16/18/20/10 failures.
mechanism: `spend-shapes.ts` case 'nested' (line 773) makes BOTH inner arms rebind ALL k locals and the outer else rebind all k directly. The #149 layout-rotation defect needs two degrees of freedom the corpus therefore never draws together: (1) the inner `if` must leave a live UNTOUCHED sibling local in the stack region it inherited from the enclosing arm — if every local is a declared result of the inner `if` there is no inherited slot left to rotate; and (2) the OUTER `if` must have NO else, so only one outer path rearranges the inherited region and the two outer paths exit at equal DEPTH but different LAYOUT. Measured directly: adding the sibling but KEEPING an outer else still yields 0 failures in 8,830 spend inputs (logs/95); adding the sibling AND dropping the outer else yields 14 failures in 120 cases (logs/96).
consequence: The strongest oracle the project owns reports clean while issue #149 is open and reproducible, and it carries a construct tag literally named `merge-nested-if` — so the corpus LOOKS like it covers nested branches. Coverage-by-tag-name is not coverage: the tag is reached on every run and is blind to the defect it appears to cover. Every future branch-layout regression in this shape ships green.
proposed_fix: Land the patch (or equivalent): add a `nested-sibling` arm style whose inner `if` rebinds only a prefix of the locals and whose OUTER `if` is rendered without an else, and add `merge-nested-sibling` to REQUIRED_TAGS so the E2 acceptance test enforces it.

title: Stateful contract whose `addOutput` continuation reads a branch-merged local alongside a live untouched sibling compiles to a script that REJECTS a valid spend — permanently locked funds; an undocumented surface of the #149 defect
repro: audits/v1-review/claude/repro/CC-013-nested-sibling-addoutput.runar.ts — deploy+call via the spend-oracle path: interpreterAccepted=true, spendAccepted=false. Reproduce en masse with the CC-013 generator patch: cd conformance && node_modules/.bin/tsx fuzzer/index.ts --spend-oracle --num 200 --seed 111
mechanism: `l0` is merged by an inner `if/else` (so the inner `if` declares results and ROLL+DROPs), `l1` (a 33-byte PubKey) is live and UNTOUCHED across that inner `if`, and the enclosing `if` has no else. The inner `if` rotates a slot it inherited from the enclosing arm; the two outer paths then exit at equal depth with different layout, and the state-continuation code emitted after OP_ENDIF is generated against only one of them. `this.addOutput(1000n, l0, l1)` consequently serialises the two values against crossed slots.
consequence: The deployed covenant fails during its own continuation with `OP_NUM2BIN requires that the size expressed in the top stack item is large enough to hold the value expressed in the second-from-top stack item` (PC 605) — NUM2BIN receives the PubKey and the bigint crossed. The source semantics ACCEPT the spend (ANF interpreter accepts) but no valid spend of the UTXO exists: funds are permanently locked. This is the same root cause as CC-001/#149, but #149 is recorded only as a stateless `assert` shape (docs/test-skips.md:111); the stateful multi-output surface is undocumented, so a fix validated only against the recorded reduction can leave this live. Reproduces on 4/4 fresh seeds (16/18/20/10 failures per 200 cases).
proposed_fix: Fix `lowerIf`'s reconcile to compare arm-exit LAYOUT (slot identity order), not just name-set and depth (same fix as CC-001), and add this stateful `addOutput` shape as a SECOND regression fixture so a fix that only repairs the stateless assert case cannot pass.

title: 183 of 578 mechanical mutants in the compiler back half are invisible to the 71-fixture golden corpus, and a 25-mutant survivor sample is invisible to every other gate too (25/25 caught by nothing)
repro: cd conformance && node_modules/.bin/tsx ../audits/v1-review/claude/repro/mut-run.ts --in ../audits/v1-review/claude/repro/mutants-sample.json --out /tmp/r.json --workers 5  # -> caught=395 survived=226; then mut-escalate.ts --sample 25 --regions branch-merge,frame-offset -> 25/25 NONE
mechanism: 621 mechanical mutants (comparison swaps, index off-by-one, boolean flips, condition negation, dropped emit statements) were generated over 05-stack-lower.ts, 06-emit.ts and src/optimizer/*, biased to lowerIf (2092-2664) and to PICK/ROLL/depth/slot arithmetic. Each was scored against all 71 conformance fixtures with a byte-exact fold-OFF hex comparison. 226 survived; excluding 37 `constant-fold.ts` mutants that are VACUOUS under my fold-OFF gate (the pass never runs — they scored 37/37 survived) the corrected figure is 183 of 578, a 68.3% mutation score. Inside lowerIf alone, 65 of 165 survive. A 25-mutant survivor sample was then escalated to branch-result-depth-invariant, branch-merged-locals-vm, state-push-framing-vm and 300 tri-modal property runs: 25 of 25 were caught by NONE of them.
consequence: The existing curated corpus (conformance/mutation, 22 mutants, all caught) measures the net's power on 22 hand-chosen bugs and reports 100%. A mechanical corpus over the same files reports 68.3%, and the survivors are not merely golden-blind — the branch-merge VM gates and the randomized absolute oracle miss them as well. The detection power of the safety net around the branch-lowering code is materially lower than the curated score implies, in exactly the region that has shipped two miscompilations.
proposed_fix: Adopt a mechanical (not only curated) mutation corpus over 05-stack-lower.ts/06-emit.ts/optimizer as a scheduled job, triage the survivor set for equivalence, and treat a non-equivalent survivor in lowerIf as a required new fixture. Note for whoever repeats this: mutants in constant-fold.ts must be scored fold-ON against a self-baseline, not against the fold-OFF goldens.

title: The terminal-assert excess-NIP cleanup path inside `lowerIf` executes ZERO times across all 71 conformance fixtures; a `depth - 1` -> `depth + 1` frame-offset mutation there is caught by no gate in the repo
repro: Copy packages/runar-compiler/src, insert `console.error('PROBE')` after 05-stack-lower.ts:2213, then run the 71-fixture gate: cd conformance && MUT_COMPILER_ENTRY=<copy>/index.js node_modules/.bin/tsx ../audits/v1-review/claude/repro/mut-gate.ts 2>&1 | grep -c PROBE  =>  0
mechanism: `if (terminalAssert && thenCtx.stackMap.depth > 1) { const excess = thenCtx.stackMap.depth - 1; for (...) { emitOp NIP; removeAtDepth(1) } }` is the then-arm cleanup for a terminal assert that leaves more than one live slot. Instrumenting the body and compiling every fixture shows the guard is never true: no fixture produces a terminal-assert `if` whose then-arm exits at depth > 1. Mutating `- 1` to `+ 1` (which would emit two extra OP_NIPs and drop two extra slots) therefore changes no golden byte, and the escalation run confirms branch-result-depth-invariant, branch-merged-locals-vm, state-push-framing-vm and 300 tri-modal runs all pass with the mutation applied.
consequence: A stack-cleanup path in the branch-lowering function is completely unexercised by the conformance corpus and by every execution gate. Any defect introduced there — including an off-by-one in the number of slots dropped, which is precisely the frame-offset class the audit brief names — ships silently. This is distinct from CC-015's aggregate score: this is a specific, named, reachable-in-principle code path with zero coverage, adjacent to the open #149 defect in the same function.
proposed_fix: Add a conformance fixture whose method ends in a terminal `assert` inside an `if` whose then-arm leaves >= 2 live slots, so the cleanup loop executes and its slot count is pinned by a golden; add the same shape to the spend-oracle shape corpus.
